bib.title: Representing Data and Engineering Features (Chapter 4, Introduction to Machine Learning with Python)

question: How should categorical and continuous features be represented and engineered so that a given model family (linear vs tree) performs well?
hypothesis: Representation and the match between features and model matter more than exact parameters.

limits: Code is scikit-learn pre-0.20 API: pandas .ix, OneHotEncoder(sparse=False) integer-only, get_feature_names, load_boston (removed from sklearn 1.2); all dated.
Single splits, single seeds, no variance; small differences (0.930 vs 0.940) rest on 285 test rows.
Authors concede feature selection rarely gives large gains on real data and the cancer-noise example is synthetic.
Does not cover target/frequency encoding, high-cardinality categories, ColumnTransformer/Pipeline or leakage in CV (selection fitted on train only is stated).
Text/code slips: Fig 4-8 code applies log twice; text says value 2 has 62 appearances but bincount shows 68; get_dummies sample says 46 columns vs X.shape 44 features.
practices: Check string categorical columns with value_counts for spelling/case variants before encoding (p.214-215).
One-hot encode nominal categoricals; do not treat integer-coded categories (e.g. workclass codes) as continuous (p.213, 218).
Call get_dummies on train and test together, or align columns, so dummy columns mean the same thing (p.217).
Separate the target (both income dummy columns) from features before training (p.216).
Bin continuous features to give linear models nonlinear power; binning is pointless for trees (p.224).
Add bin x feature interactions to give each bin its own slope (p.225-226).
Add polynomial/interaction features for linear and naive Bayes models; trees find interactions themselves (p.231-236).
Apply log(X+1) to skewed count features (and possibly log(y+1) target) for linear models/NNs; irrelevant for trees (p.234-235).
Fit feature selection on the training split only (p.236).
Use expert knowledge features (holidays, hour, weekday); for time series split chronologically (p.242-244).
Trees cannot extrapolate beyond the training feature range; do not feed raw timestamps (p.245).

terms.definition: replace a categorical variable with one new 0/1 feature per category; exactly one is 1 (also one-out-of-N, dummy variables)
k categories encoded into k-1 features to avoid a rank-deficient data matrix
split a continuous feature into a fixed number of intervals and represent a point by its bin
the question of how to represent your data best for a particular application
test each feature individually for a significant relationship with the target and keep the most significant
use a supervised model's feature importances to keep the most important features, considering all at once
start with all features, build a model, discard the least important, repeat until a prespecified number remain
